head_commit.message:
chore: move onto provider SDK 0.13.0 and prepare v0.3.0 (#6)

The next dekopon release deletes `resolve-command` from the broker host and the
`CompatCapability` decoder that lets an old manifest's `idempotency` field
through, so a component built against 0.10.0 stops loading. This is the rebuild.

- `dekopon-provider-sdk` and `dekopon-provider-http` move to `=0.13.0`, with the
  SDK's `clap` feature. The SDK re-exports the exact clap it was built against,
  so no clap dependency is declared here: two clap versions in one guest would
  render two different help pages.
- `Idempotency` is gone from the SDK. The classification is deleted from every
  capability literal and from the `write` helper's parameter list.
- The vendored WIT moves to `dekopon:provider@0.3.0` verbatim, and the world
  includes `provider-cli` rather than `provider-commands`.
- `Provider::resolve_command` becomes `Provider::run_command`, exported with
  `export_provider_with_cli!`. The `gh` word now behaves like the upstream
  command-line tool: `gh --help` and `gh pr view --help` render on stdout at
  status 0, `gh bogus` and a missing argument render clap's usage error on
  stderr at status 2, and `--body-file -` reads the value piped into the word.
  The hand-rolled flag parser is replaced by one declared clap tree.
- Every capability identifier is named once in `ids`, read by `capabilities()`,
  `invoke_with`, and the command tree, so a rename is a build error rather than
  an exit code a model discovers mid-session.
- `dekopon-provider-http` 0.13.0 deleted `Response::header_values` as an
  unreferenced public item; it is two callers' worth of code and lives here now.
- Toolchain moves in lockstep: Rust 1.98.1, wit-bindgen 0.62.0, wasm-tools
  1.259.0, in `build.sh`, both workflows, and the README.
- The pr-summarizer-linter example is brought back to a configuration 0.13.0
  will load: `kind: Capability` and `kind: Provider` catalog documents are
  refused outright now, and `idempotency` is no longer a `ConstraintSet` field.

Carries the intent of #5: argv holds only the arguments after the command word,
so `gh pr view 7` arrives as `["pr", "view", "7"]`. The clap tree parses it that
way through `Command::no_binary_name`, and the test asserting the wire shape
directly comes with it.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix: read argv without the command word, as the SDK sends it

head_commit.message:
fix: read argv without the command word, as the SDK sends it

`resolve` split `argv[0]` off as the command word, but no layer ever puts it
there. `Provider::resolve_command` selects the word before the call ("`argv`
contains only the arguments after it") and the broker protocol's `RunCommand`
frame carries the word in its own field, precisely so the guest cannot get a
second copy of a routing decision already made.

So `gh pr view 7 -R o/r` arrives as `["pr", "view", "7", "-R", "o/r"]`, the
parser dropped `pr`, read `view` as the area and `7` as the verb, and every
`gh <area> <verb>` failed with a usage error and exit 2. The parser was ported
from a dekopon-shell builtin that received the word; the shift came in with the
port.

The tests hid it by prepending `"gh"` to every argv, so they exercised a shape
the SDK never sends. They now pass argv as the guest receives it, with a named
regression test for the wire shape and one for an empty argv.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ui7zKZ6SuRgEYs4i818ApX

workflow_runs.name: Release
workflow_runs.display_title: Finish the move out of the Dekopon tree (#1)

head_commit.message:
Finish the move out of the Dekopon tree (#1)

* fix: depend on published dekopon crates instead of a deleted branch

Both SDK crates were pinned to branch `feat/broker-command-protocol`, which GitHub deleted
when dekopon PR #90 merged. Cargo resolves a `branch =` dependency by fetching that ref, so
this repository could not build anywhere the git cache was cold — which is every CI runner.
The one CI run it has ever had failed before it got far enough to notice.

`dekopon-provider-sdk` and `dekopon-provider-http` are both published at 0.9.0, and that
release already carries the command-word surface this provider needs: `command_words`,
`resolve_command`, `CommandInvocation`, and `export_provider_with_commands!`. So there is no
reason to take a git dependency at all. Pinned exactly and together, because the two are
published from one workspace at one version and a skew between them would be invisible.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* build: restore the reproducibility harness the move dropped

Leaving the tree cost this provider its build harness. `build.sh` had become a plain `cargo
build` plus `wasm-tools component new`: no toolchain pin, no `-Cmetadata` normalization, no
path remapping. That is a regression against its own in-tree ancestor, which still calls
dekopon's shared `examples/providers/build-component.sh` and always did.

This is a self-contained port of that driver, keeping every mechanism: the `rustc` proxy that
rewrites `-Cmetadata` to a fixed salt, the three `--remap-path-prefix` entries,
`-Ccodegen-units=1`, `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` so a stray `.cargo/config.toml` cannot outrank
them, the exact rustc gate, and the final scan that fails the build if a local path survives
into the component. The salt stays `dekopon-provider-repro-v1` — it already includes the
package name, so it cannot collide, and changing it would forfeit the comparison for nothing.

It also takes an output path and honours `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, which is what lets CI and the
release workflow build the component twice and byte-compare.

Verified: the in-tree driver reproduces dekopon's shipped `gh-provider.wasm` byte for byte on
this machine, and this port lands on the same bytes from two independent target directories.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: fix the toolchain install and prove the component

`rustup toolchain install --component clippy rustfmt` reads the second name as a toolchain,
not a component, so rustup rejected the command and every later step skipped. That is the
whole of this repository's CI history: one run, seven seconds, red. dekopon-provider-turso-sql
hit the same bug and fixed it the same way.

Installing a toolchain is also not pinning to one. Without `rustup override set` the pin was
decorative and every cargo step ran on the runner default — and the pin itself was wrong,
1.89.0 being the crate's MSRV rather than the toolchain `build.sh` requires.

The larger gap was that nothing checked the artifact. Out of tree there is no shared WIT file
keeping the mirrors honest and no in-tree workflow rebuilding the checked-in component, so
both gates have to be re-created here:

- the WIT mirrors are fetched from dekopon at the release `Cargo.lock` resolved and compared,
  so an upstream interface change fails loudly instead of yielding a component that mismatches
  the host it gets loaded into;
- the component is built, rebuilt into a clean target directory, and byte-compared;
- `wasm-bindgen`, `js-sys` and `wasi` are rejected — the ambient escape hatches wasm32 offers
  a provider that is supposed to reach the world only through declared imports;
- the core module's imports must be exactly `dekopon:http/client@1.0.0`, so a new authority
  cannot arrive unreviewed.

The release workflow gains the same rebuild-and-compare before it attests. Reproducibility and
provenance answer different questions — who built this, and what it was built from — and a tag
should not ship without both.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: adopt the pr-summarizer-linter walkthrough

The end-to-end example is built on this provider's capabilities — nineteen of them, a Cedar
policy naming them individually, and an agent prompt written around `gh pr view` and friends.
It exercises this component, not dekopon's own machinery, so it belongs beside the thing it
demonstrates and moves with it.

Paths that pointed across the old tree are now absolute links to dekopon, and the two that
stayed relative resolve inside this repository: the component at the root, and the provider
README the walkthrough refers to. Nothing about the deployment changes — the broker still
loads a component from a directory it owns.

The README's "Using it" section pointed at `examples/rubber-stamper`, which no longer exists
in either repository; it points here now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
feat: the GitHub provider, out of the Dekopon tree

Nineteen narrow repository, pull-request, and issue capabilities, plus the
`gh` command word that maps GitHub-CLI spellings onto them.

The subcommand table lived in `dekopon-shell` as 959 lines of GitHub
knowledge inside the core interpreter. It moves here whole — every
spelling, the --approve/--comment/--request-changes split, the rejected
flags, and the `gh api` refusal — now that a provider can export
`resolve-command`.

Moving it also removes a class of drift. The table and the capability list
it maps onto are compiled together, so a capability renamed in lib.rs and
forgotten in commands.rs is a build error rather than an exit code 127 a
model discovers mid-session. Nothing checked that before.

The SDK dependencies are pinned to the branch introducing
dekopon:provider@0.2.0; they move to crates.io once dekopon publishes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
